From: Kevin Park <kevin.park@medbot.ai>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Latency SLO tiering and evidence collection for order form amend

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we work through final MSA/SOW attachments and the order form, legal has asked us to define latency SLOs by workload tier (interactive vs batch) and a clear evidence and audit window for the first 12 months. Two asks from our side:

1) Can Redwood commit to a p95 latency for the interactive tier (our expected traffic pattern is small-context chat at ~1.2k reqs/min)? We want to see committed numbers for p50/p95 and an explicit fallback policy if regional capacity is constrained.
2) What evidence do you provide for monthly SLO measurement? Specifically: sampling cadence, retention of raw latency traces, and whether we can request a historical audit (30/60/90 days).

I've attached our current MSA/SOW excerpt for reference (MedBot-SLA-SOW_v2.pdf). We also need suggested order form language that calls out the latency tiers and the audit pull process.

Can you loop in whoever owns order form language and legal? We hope to get a redline by next week.

Best,
Kevin Park
Head of Ops, MedBot AI
attachments: MedBot-SLA-SOW_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
To: Kevin Park <kevin.park@medbot.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Latency SLO tiering and evidence collection for order form amend

Kevin —

Thanks for the clear ask and the attached MSA excerpt. High-level answers up front:

- Interactive tier: we can propose a committed p95 target of 250ms for small-context generative requests (<=512 tokens) with a documented regional fallback to a compatible model variant when capacity constraints hit.
- Batch tier: we recommend a p95 of 1200ms for batched embedding/rerank jobs with different throughput economics.
- Evidence: we provide monthly SLO reports (p50/p95/p99), raw latency trace exports (retained 90 days by default), and we support ad-hoc audit pulls for up to 90 days upon request (we'll outline the SLA process and an expected 5 business-day window for audits).

Next steps I suggest:
1) I’m attaching our latency evidence template (redwood_latency-evidence-template.xlsx) so you can see the fields and formats we export.
2) Rishi — can you review the proposed numbers and confirm whether 250ms p95 is acceptable as a committed interactive SLO for enterprise order form language?
3) Ben — can you prepare a short order form appendix we can drop into their order form that calls out definitions, measurement method, audit request process, and fallback policy?

We'll aim to produce a redline (order form appendix + SLA exhibit) by EOD Wednesday so Kevin can circulate to MedBot legal.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_latency-evidence-template.xlsx (xlsx)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Latency SLO tiering and evidence collection for order form amend

Sofia / Ben —

250ms p95 for interactive (<=512 tokens) is aggressive but feasible on our dedicated pools with the following caveats to be explicit in the order form:

- Measurement definition: p95 measured at the ingress gateway for completed generation responses, excluding client timeouts and retries.
- Exceptions: scheduled maintenance windows and force-maj events excluded; regional capacity fallback allowed (we will provide auto-failover to a compatible model with equivalent correctness but higher latency).
- Breach handling: credits based on token-level economic impact; first material breach triggers investigation and a 30-day remediation plan.

Laura — can you draft 2 short variants of the order form sentence: one that commits 250ms p95 with a narrow exception window (99.7% uptime target) and one that commits a 300ms p95 with a wider exception tolerance (99.5%). We'll present both to the customer.

Ben — please include the audit pull SLA text: request via support ticket, 5 business-day turnaround, delivery as CSV + raw traces for the requested window (up to 90 days).

Rishi
VP, Product Ops (inference)
Redwood Inference

From: Kevin Park <kevin.park@medbot.ai>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
Cc: ops@medbot.ai
Date: Thu, 25 Nov 2026 09:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Latency SLO tiering and evidence collection for order form amend

Thanks, Sofia / Rishi —

The 250ms p95 proposal looks good as long as the order form clearly calls out the exception and fallback behavior. Two clarifications from our legal/compliance team:

- Audit scope: we need confirmation that raw traces used for p95 calculation include request timestamps, model variant id, and region tag.
- Historical pulls: for the pilot we’ll ask for 60 days, but contractually would like an option to request up to 90 days during first year.

If you can send the two wording variants and the audit pull text I’ll get legal to prioritize a quick review. Also send a DocuSign link when the exhibit is ready.

—Kevin

Kevin —

Appended below are the two short order form variants and the audit pull language we discussed. I've attached a draft SLA exhibit and a plain-text appendix you can paste into the order form. Ben and Laura will track legal redlines.

Order form language (variant A — narrower exception, higher commitment):
"Interactive SLO: Redwood shall use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain p95 request latency <= 250ms for interactive requests (<=512 tokens). Measurement is at the Redwood ingress and excludes scheduled maintenance and force majeure. In the event of regional capacity constraint, Redwood will automatically route requests to an available compatible model variant; routing may increase latency but preserve request completion. Uptime target: 99.7%"

Order form language (variant B — broader tolerance):
"Interactive SLO: Redwood shall use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain p95 request latency <= 300ms for interactive requests (<=512 tokens). Measurement is at the Redwood ingress and excludes scheduled maintenance and force majeure. In the event of regional capacity constraint, Redwood will automatically route requests to an available compatible model variant; routing may increase latency but preserve request completion. Uptime target: 99.5%"

Audit pull SLA (to include in exhibit):
"Audit pull process: Customer may submit a request via Redwood Support to receive raw latency traces and aggregate SLO reports for a specified date range. Requested fields: request_id, request_timestamp_utc, model_variant_id, region, latency_ms, status_code. Standard retention is 90 days; initial pilot access will include 60-day historical pulls. Redwood will acknowledge a valid request within 2 business days and deliver data within 5 business days. Extraordinary requests may incur a data-delivery fee, subject to prior notice."
